content.text:
Ceate an SVG of an awkward family portrait of robots. Give each robot a distinct personality, and suggest their relationships through poses and composition. No text.

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.11.1 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

content.thinking:
I'm creating an SVG family portrait of robots with distinct personalities and awkward poses.

I'm reviewing the strict file limits and tool constraints. The deliverables must stay under 2 MB each and videos under 10 seconds. I'll keep source code in the working directory and delete intermediate files.

The SVG will be the primary deliverable, since it is an allowed image format. A PNG preview may be rendered for convenience.

The portrait must be visually distinctive rather than generic clipart. Each robot will carry a unique personality through its pose and composition.

The portrait follows a stiff formal studio composition. Robots are mismatched in height and design, suggesting different manufacturers. The patriarch robot stands rigidly with one arm awkwardly around the mother's shoulder.

The patriarch robot has a square head and rigid rectangular eyes. A wire tie or bow adds to his formal stiffness.

The mother robot is sleeker and curved. Her hands are folded precisely but one finger twitches. Her LED smile is slightly too wide and asymmetric. She tries to hold the family together.

The teenage robot slouches with crossed arms. It looks away from the camera and wears headphones.

The teenage robot carries a rebellious paint job and stands with one leg cocked, clearly unwilling to pose.

The little kid robot is small and round. It waves an arm while the rest of the family stays still, or clings to its mother with huge eyes. It may hold a broken toy and show a gap-toothed LED smile.

The grandparent robot is antique and riveted in brass or copper tones. It sits in a chair that is too small or ornate.

The grandparent robot has one eye replaced with a mismatched lens. It stoops and holds a charging cable as a cane. The chair is crooked.

A quadruped pet robot wanders into the frame. It looks the wrong way or sits on someone's foot.

The portrait uses uneven spacing and tilted heads to create awkwardness.

The composition breaks into an almost-triangle shape. The teenager sits outside the group by half a step.

A wrinkled studio curtain forms the backdrop. Flash highlights and a formal gray background add to the stiff studio feel.

One robot's hand rests on another's shoulder, but the fingers are too wide for that shoulder width. This suggests inter-manufacturer incompatibility.

The little robot stands on a visible box or stool.

The grandparent's chair is anachronistic to the studio setting. Cables tangle between family members to suggest messy connections. The pet robot is mid-yawn or watching a fly.

I will hand-code the SVG directly rather than use image generation tools, since those produce raster images and not SVG.

The SVG will use a wide studio portrait ratio around 1400 by 1000 pixels. The background will be warm gray-taupe with a subtle vignette and painted canvas texture. The floor will be darker wood or mottled. Each robot will carry a distinct material finish.

The grandparent robot uses aged brass and copper patina with round porthole eyes. The dad robot is matte charcoal with a safety-yellow accent stripe and rectangular fluorescent eye bars. The mom robot has cream and soft coral enamel with circular eyes that glow warmly. The teenager is matte black with an electric magenta underglow, a scratched sticker panel, and an asymmetric hair antenna. The child robot is primary-colored toy plastic with oversized sky-blue and yellow limbs. The pet robot is either a small oxidized green beetle-bot or a dachshund-shaped quadruped.

The dad robot's left hand rests on the mother's shoulder, but one finger sticks up as if he does not know how hands work on fabric. The mother's smile is a perfect arc while her eyes are slightly too wide. The grandparent robot faces the dad rather than the camera and leans at five degrees; his chair leg rests on the mother's dress panel. The teenager stands with arms crossed and weight on the back foot, chin down, one eye looking sideways at the camera like a monocle while the other is powered down or turned away. One foot steps on the backdrop stand so the curtain pulls.

The child robot stands on a stack of rectangular manuals, waving with both arms and mouth open in a beep. One shoe light blinks a different color.

The pet robot squeezes its head between the child and the teenager, sticking out a tongue-antenna and wagging its tail cable into the frame edge.

The studio key light comes from the upper left, casting consistent shadows to the right.

The awkwardness will come from poses rather than broken perspective. A softbox reflection might catch the grandparent's brass dome eye. The height hierarchy is now defined: the grandfather sits low, the mother sits at eye level, the father stands tall behind them, the teenager is nearly as tall but slouches so their head drops below the father's, and the child remains short despite standing on books.

The eye-line is deliberately broken: the child’s eyes sit higher than expected from the books, while the teenager’s eyes drop lower from slouching, so the almost-straight line of heads fails. The SVG will use gradients for metallic surfaces, filters for soft shadows and subtle noise, and clean geometric construction with rivets, panel lines, and joints. Eye glows will be created with filters. The viewBox is fixed at 1600 by 1100 pixels, and the backdrop will be a full rectangle with a gradient from warm gray-taupe to darker gray-taupe and an elliptical vignette.

The backdrop will use a seamless cyclorama curve rather than a flat rectangle. The floor will be a wood-like ellipse or trapezoid with a warm gray-green gradient. The curtain folds will be slightly asymmetric, with one band bunched awkwardly. Robots will be drawn from back to front.

The grandparent robot is now defined as "The Original Model." Its dome head is a brass diving bell with darker oxidized patches. Two round glass eyes sit at slightly different sizes, with the left one larger and warmer. A bushy mustache is made of frayed copper wire. The barrel chest shows rivet rows. The wooden spindle chair is too small, so his elbows stick out past the armrests. He stacks his hands on a telescoping cane between his knees. One foot turns inward. Patina and dents add to the aged look.

The grandparent robot is proud and patient, with one ear horn cocked toward the family as if slightly deaf. The chair sits too far left, leaving a gap between him and his wife; his cane angles toward her to bridge it.

The dad robot is tall and rectangular, standing at center-back. He is the "Middle Management Unit," painted charcoal with a thin yellow safety stripe that looks crooked because he applied it himself. His head is a monitor-like rounded rectangle flush with his shoulders, with no neck.

The dad robot's eyes are two horizontal cyan slits, perfectly level and unblinking. His mouth is a thin straight line of LEDs that does not quite form a smile. His right arm hangs at his side with a slightly clenched fist. His left arm reaches toward the mother's far shoulder, but the elbow is stiff at forty degrees and one finger does not quite touch. His legs are straight with feet too close together, giving an attention-at-attention look. A small pocket square shaped like a folded schematic and a tiny antenna tie complete his outfit.

The dad robot is trying very hard to look like a normal dad. He stands so straight he looks uncomfortable. His head is a half inch higher than the backdrop's ideal center.

The mom robot sits on a low bench in the center. She is the "Domestic Series, hospitality firmware." Her rounded shoulders are cream enamel with coral joint caps and a soft apron-like front panel that is slightly stained. Her head is oval with large circular eyes that have warm amber irises and a tiny highlight. The left eyebrow-panel is raised higher, suggesting uncertainty.

The mother's smile is a wide curved slot that is slightly too big for her face, revealing a row of even white LED teeth as if she is overcommitting to "say cheese." Her hands are folded in her lap, but the top hand gently touches the child's back to anchor the wiggling kid. Her lower chassis flares into a skirt-like shape, and one side is caught under the grandfather's chair leg. A small bouquet of wire flowers pinned to her chest droops slightly, with one bloom bent. She is the glue holding the family together, performing warmth with a little strain.

The mother robot leans three degrees toward the child and two degrees toward the grandfather, making her the hinge of the family. Her knees angle toward the kid.

The teenager robot is tall and lean in matte black with a chipped panel revealing orange primer. A swept antenna "bang" falls over one eye. The visible eye is half-lidded with a magenta ring, unimpressed, while the covered eye glows faintly through the bangs. The mouth is a tiny flat dash almost off. Arms are crossed tight with one shoulder higher. A draped cable-knit suggests a hoodie.

The teenager's hoodie is oversized and thrown over the chassis. One sleeve is pushed up and the drawstrings are uneven. His legs are split: one straight, one bent with the foot turned out, leaning against nothing or the backdrop pole. The sneakers are chunky with mismatched laces, one undone. He is present under protest. A full gap separates him from the dad, and his crossed arms form a closed shape against the family's open cluster. His head tilts away.

The child robot sits at front center-left as the "Early learning chassis, overclocked." Its body is glossy toy plastic in sky blue with yellow limbs and red cheek circles, one smudged. It has an enormous head and star-shaped catchlights in its eyes that look straight into the lens with pure delight. Its mouth is an open rectangle beep with one missing tooth-LED. Both arms are raised, though a ghost arm for motion blur was considered too messy.

The child robot stands on two thick, unevenly stacked manuals with blank covers. One foot glows with a light-up sole. A tiny propeller beanie or bent antenna with a bead completes the look. The child waves and holds the mother's finger, breaking the top line of the composition. The books tilt the child toward the mother, who steadies them. The child has joy and no concept of the photo's seriousness. The pet robot is placed at front right as "The good one."

The pet robot is a low, long dachshund-roomba hybrid in oxidized teal. It has six little wheels half-hidden, a snout with a whisker antenna, and one floppy ear panel beside one perked. Its rear is scooted so it sits on the teenager's foot. The head turns upward toward the camera, and its eyes look slightly different directions or at a moth near the softbox. A charging cable with a plug forms its tail, wagging mid-wag and looping toward the bottom right corner. A small pink ribbon cable serves as its tongue. The pet is beloved chaos that breaks the formal bottom edge of the arrangement.

The seamless cyclorama shows a wrinkle behind the grandfather. A piece of gaffer tape lies on the floor near the dad's foot. Softbox reflections appear only on metallic surfaces. Each figure casts a contact shadow, larger and softer for standing figures. The corner of a silver reflector disc intrudes at the top left.

The family shares a circular chest "power heart" that unifies their distinct styles. The color story splits into two threads: brass and yellow for the dad and grandfather, and coral and magenta for the mother and teenager. The child's red cheeks and the pet's teal echo the warm thread. The pet could also wear a coral collar to show ownership. The composition will use slightly uneven spacing for a relaxed, natural feel.

The SVG will be hand-authored rather than generated by Python. It will be organized into five layers: definitions for gradients and filters, the cyclorama background, floor shadows drawn before the robots, the figures back to front, and foreground details like the pet tail and child's waving hand. The file may run 1500 to 3000 lines long.

I am checking the workspace first. I also need to verify whether ffmpeg can render SVG to PNG, since no external packages are available.

Standard Python and Node cannot rasterize SVG without installing packages, so I will deliver the SVG itself. I am checking whether system tools like rsvg-convert or qlmanage can render it to a video.

I will deliver a single SVG in output/ and skip any PNG conversion. I am also considering a brief SMIL animation to animate the child’s wave, the pet’s tail, a blinking LED, and the teenager’s half-roll.

The static SVG must look complete on its own, since the published result might be flattened. The SMIL animation is a bonus that captures the family’s inability to stay still.

The animation plan is now specific. The child’s hand will rotate slightly, the pet’s tail will wag, and one eye will blink or a missing LED will flicker. The teenager’s hoodie drawstring sway is too much and will be omitted. The mother’s smile stays fixed, the dad’s finger twitches once, and the grandfather’s ear horn remains still. A status LED on the pet will also blink. These gestures are kept gentle so the static frame reads as a complete portrait. I am now moving into careful coordinate planning and writing the SVG.

The SVG will use a 16:10 viewBox of 1600 by 1000. I am mapping approximate head centers for the grandfather and father to anchor the composition.

I am locking in the exact coordinates for each figure. The mother sits at (620, 480), the teenager at (1120, 360), the child at (780, 620) on books, and the pet at (980, 860). The floor line is fixed at y=860. I am also defining the grandfather’s chair and the dad’s standing position so the figures overlap naturally and read as a pushed-together family rather than a lineup.

The exact x and y ranges for each figure are now fixed. The dad’s arm will rest over the mother’s shoulder. The teenager leans out from behind the pet, who overlaps his left foot and sits just in front of the child. The final layer order is backdrop, grandfather, dad, teenager, mother, child with books, pet, and floor shadow.

The dad’s arm will be drawn as a separate group in front of the mother so his hand rests on her shoulder. The grandfather’s cane may cross in front of his legs but behind the mother. The style is mid-century modern editorial vector: soft gradients, clean shapes, limited palette, and chunky elegant geometry.

The figures will be built from rounded rectangles, ellipses, and precise paths. I am choosing a lineless look with subtle value contrast rather than heavy outlines. Each robot will get a thin 0.5–1 px stroke in a darker shade of its body color for readability. Highlights will be drawn as separate shapes.

I am adding an SVG filter to simulate film grain and a subtle warm color grade, so the portrait feels like a printed photograph. I am also drafting a soft shadow filter for the figures.

Contact shadows will be drawn as floor ellipses rather than filter drop shadows for better control. The SVG will be written directly as a raw file in src/ and copied to output/, since the artwork itself is the source.

I am now locking in the exact color values for each robot. The backdrop cyclorama will use warm paper tones from #e4dcd2 down to #6e675f. The grandfather’s brass palette includes #c4964a mid-tone, #7a5a28 shadow, and #6e8a72 patina. The dad’s body will be #4a5560 with a dark #2c333a accent.

The dad’s palette is now complete with a #6d7a86 highlight, #e6b325 stripe, #7ee0e8 eye, and #1e4d6b tie. The mother’s enamel skin, coral accents, amber eye, and apron panel are locked in. The teenager’s black body, dusty indigo hoodie, magenta eye, and red sneakers are mapped out. The child’s blue tones, yellow highlights, red cheeks, and white iris are set. The pet’s teal shell, dark belly, and light underbelly finish the color chart.

The pet’s tongue will be #e8889a and its collar will match the mother’s coral at #d4685a. The style is a cohesive studio photograph of sculpted robots. I will build the SVG in parts and review it visually, using system tools like qlmanage or Chrome headless to preview without downloading anything.

A rough ASCII layout is locking the vertical stack. Dad and grandfather sit near y=200–280, the teenager near y=400, the mother near y=520, the child with books near y=640, and the pet near y=760. The floor line is fixed at y=880.

The left-heavy composition is intentional. The teenager’s isolation is the story, balanced by the pet bridging toward them and the child’s wave pulling the eye across. The reflector on the left and the tail on the right keep the frame from feeling like a lineup. Staggered depths will prevent a flat line-up: the grandfather sits slightly behind the picture plane, and the dad stands furthest back.

The depth layer order is now fixed: teenager mid, mother mid-front, child front, pet frontmost. All adult heads are roughly 110–130 px wide, with the grandfather’s dome slightly larger. The child’s head is 120 px but sits oversized relative to his body, while the pet stays low and long. Exact vertical scales are set: dad stands at 640 px, the slouching teenager at 580 px, the seated mother at 420–840 px, the seated grandfather at 310–840 px, and the child with books at 580–800 px.

The SVG will be fully self-contained with no external fonts or images. The child’s wave gesture will begin from a raised position so the static frame reads as the finished portrait, and the animation will add motion from that pose. I am now looking for a specific visual detail that will make this awkward family portrait memorable.

The concept title is "Hold still." The portrait captures the instant after the photographer says that command but before the shutter fires. Each robot interprets it differently: the grandfather drifts away from the lens, the dad locks every servo with a smile that never arrives, the mother holds the family together emotionally, the teenager refuses to participate, the child heard "cheese," and the dog-bot ignores the instruction to stand still and instead inspects the teenager's untied shoe.

A shared chest-core design unifies the family despite different manufacturers. Each robot has two eyes, a mouth slot, and a small circular status lamp. The lamp color reveals emotional state: amber for the grandfather, flickering green for the dad’s anxiety, warm rose for the mother, dim blue for the teenager, and rapid rainbow for the child.

The pet’s status lamp will pulse happy green. Each robot gets a unique antenna that echoes the family genealogy: the grandfather’s ear trumpet, the dad’s short matched pair, the mother’s soft loop bun, the teenager’s long swept bead, the child’s wobbling spring, and the pet’s whisker. These shared antennae create a visual relationship across the portrait.

The mother’s shoulder is slightly raised, her hand wrapping the child’s torso protectively. The child holds the apron cord and waves, attached to mom and performing for the camera. The grandfather’s open palm hovers near the mother’s arm, a few inches away, capturing his hesitation to connect. The teenager’s crossed arms are loose, not a tight fist, showing partial sulkiness.

The pet sits on the teenager’s untied shoe, and a toe is angled to give it room. The dad stands closer to the mother than to the teenager, widening the gap on the teen’s side; the teen angles away to notice. The grandfather looks at the dad rather than the lens, carrying a silent critique of posture. The mother glances at the lens but her pupils drift toward the child, showing divided attention. The child looks straight into the lens with pure focus.

Eye directions will carry the emotional story. The grandfather’s pupils shift toward the dad. The dad’s eyes sit perfectly centered, unnaturally symmetrical. The mother’s pupils drift slightly right toward the child and the lens. The teenager’s eye looks down at the pet or off-camera, revealing either softness or refusal.

The teenager’s uncovered eye will look off-frame right, showing disdain, while the head tilt also reveals awareness of the pet. The child’s pupils will sit centered and slightly up to engage the camera. The pet’s eyes will look up toward the shoelace. A single softbox in the upper left will cast identical catchlights on every robot, unifying the lighting.

Catchlights will vary by robot. The child’s are larger and shinier, the grandfather’s are distorted by curved brass rims, the teenager’s is a thin magenta crescent, and the dad’s sit on emissive slits. Shadows fall to the lower right with slight rightward shifts. The grandfather’s chest panel will show rivets, a patched brass plate, and scratches.

The dad’s chest panel will show a blank name-badge rectangle and a pen-shaped stylus in a chest slot, with the yellow stripe not meeting at the back seam. The mother’s coral wrist will carry a bracelet of washer-rings made by the child, one washer slightly larger.

The teenager’s chest panel will show chipped paint, a magenta pin-back button with no text, a headphone band doubled as a welded antenna, uneven drawstrings with one missing aglet, and a visible sock-cable above the sneaker. The child’s arm will be a slightly different yellow to mark a recent replacement after a fall, and a sticker residue peeling off his knee will carry a bandage decal. The pet’s ear will have a chewed corner, its collar tag will be a blank circle, and one wheel will be a different shade. The design is now fully detailed and ready to build.

I will generate the SVG with Python to handle repetitive elements like rivets and gradients, while hand-tuning the main paths. The script will be structured for easy re-rendering. I am also checking which preview tools are available on macOS to verify the output.

I will render the SVG to PNG with qlmanage and read it back for review, since no browser MCP is available. The plan is to write the generator, preview the image, critique it, iterate until it looks like a real illustration, copy the final file to output/, clean intermediates, and summarize. The finished SVG should stay under 2 MB.

I am organizing the SVG into grouped layers with transforms. Each robot will be drawn in local coordinates anchored at its floor contact point. This keeps positioning simple and the file compact.

I will use absolute coordinates rather than local transforms to avoid mis-translating the robots. The style will be a polished flat design with gradients, inspired by high-end editorial illustration.

I am locking in the studio background. The wall will use a gradient rectangle, and the floor will be a dark ellipse from y=680 downward to keep the composition clean. I am also committing to bold, readable shapes and avoiding tiny details that would blur.

A curved highlight will sweep where the wall meets the floor. A radial vignette will darken the edges. The left curtain will be a rough, uneven wavy bundle in a darker shade; the right side stays clean and asymmetric. An elliptical silver reflector disc will peek in from the top-left corner. A small dark gaffer-tape rectangle will sit near the center, partly under the dad’s shadow, marking the spot where he missed the instruction by a few inches.

The grandfather sits left-center in a slightly turned wooden chair. Its four legs are splayed and uneven, with one leg missing a felt pad. The seat cushion is thin and worn, bearing a simple geometric oval pattern. The chair back has a rounded top rail and two vertical slats. He is seated upright but his shoulders roll forward from age.

The grandfather’s dome head sits almost on his torso, held by a short brass ring. Its surface is an ellipse with a left-to-right brass gradient and a top highlight. The face plate is a darker circle in the front. His eyes are two circles: the viewer’s left eye is smaller and slightly higher, both rimmed in copper with pupils looking right. A single curved brass brow sits heavier over the smaller eye to show squint. His mustache is a bushy asymmetric copper wire, and his mouth is mostly hidden by it with only a small straight vent visible.

The grandfather’s right ear will be a small brass horn angled toward the family, not the camera. This matches his pupils looking right at the dad and mom, and it creates overlap with the dad’s space.

The grandfather’s torso is barrel-shaped and wider than his head. A horizontal band runs across the chest with six rivets. An amber lamp sits in the center, and a newer patched brass plate with four rivets sits on the lower left. His arms are thick and segmented; both hands grip the cane between his knees, angled toward the family. The top hand is misaligned with overlapping fingers. His legs are short in the seat, knees apart, with vertical lower legs and heavy boots. One boot has a mismatched lace or buckle.

The grandfather’s outer hand will grip the cane while his inner hand hovers near the mother, palm slightly open, leaving a visible gap between his elbow and her arm. This reads as an almost held arm. Exact coordinates for the grandfather are now locked in: head center at (340, 400), torso at (340, 560), seat at y=680, feet at y=860.

Dad will stand behind and slightly right of the mother, so only his head, shoulders, arms, and a sliver of his right-side legs are visible. His head center is at (760, 250) and he is the tallest robot. The head is a rounded rectangle measuring 150 by 120 with a corner radius of 28.

The dad’s head is wide and screen-like, resting on a collar plate with no neck. His face shows two horizontal cyan eye slits with glass covers and diagonal highlights. A darker brow ridge sits above them. His mouth is eight tiny squares in a row; only the middle four glow dimly, making it look like a smile that failed to boot. Ventilation slots line the sides of his head. Two short antennas with ball tips sit symmetrically on either side, but the left one has a third tiny stub where an antenna broke and was trimmed, adding a humanizing flaw.

Dad’s torso is a broad suit-like shape with an inverted trapezoid body. A lapel panel and a yellow measuring-tape sash sit across his chest at a slight tilt, suggesting he thought it was straight. A blank badge rectangle sits on the upper left chest, also tilted in the opposite direction. A small green chest lamp and a stylus rest in his breast pocket. A dark teal tie hangs from the collar with a circular clip, slightly off-center.

Dad’s right arm hangs at his side in the gap between mom and teen. The blocky fist is not fully closed, curling as if he does not know what to do with it. The arm is long and the hand ends past his thigh from stiff posture.

Dad’s left arm reaches across to mom’s far shoulder. The elbow sticks out in a triangle. The forearm comes down onto her shoulder. The blocky four-fingered hand rests there but the index finger is lifted slightly.

Dad’s wrist is bent at an unnatural angle. Only one of his feet is visible beside mom, placed slightly too far right so he looks off-balance. The mother’s head center is set at (640, 470).

The mother sits on a lower bench than the grandfather, so her head at y=470 falls in front of the standing dad’s chest-shoulder line. Her head is a soft oval measuring 100 by 110. A loose copper bun with one escaping strand forms her hair. Her face plate is cream.

The mother’s eyes are large white circles with amber irises and pupils shifted toward the child. Her brows are thin coral arcs, with the left one higher to show worry. Soft blushes sit on her cheeks, and her smile is a wide arc with six rectangular teeth; one tooth glows dimmer. Her ears are small rounded discs.

Her torso is a soft rounded vase wider at the hips. A coral collar sits around her neck, and her chest stays cream.

A glowing rose-gold chest lamp sits on the mother’s torso. Her apron is a pale pink rectangle tied with an uneven side bow and a tiny screwdriver handle peeking from its pocket. A wire flower with three loops and a bent stem rests on her chest. Her left arm wraps toward the child, its hand visible on the child’s side with gentle curved fingers.

The mother’s right arm rests in her lap, and the grandfather’s hand hovers near that forearm. A bracelet of washers sits on her left wrist. Her skirt is a full bell from waist to seat, with two thin metal legs peeking out; one leg has a mismatched foot cap. The image-left edge of the skirt stays clear of the grandfather’s boot area. Her knees are together and angled toward the child, while the child’s books overlap the front of her skirt.

The teen’s head sits at (1180, 340), tall and to the right of the family cluster. The gap between dad’s visible arm and the teen’s crossed arms is about 80–100 pixels.

The head is a narrow rounded rectangle tilted slightly toward the image right. Thick curved antenna strands sweep across the left eye from the top of the head, hiding the family-facing eye. The visible eye is half-lidded with a magenta iris looking further right off camera.

The teen’s face shows an asymmetric frown dash and a chunky headphone band with one ear cup; the other ear has a washer earring matching the mother’s bracelet, which the teen would deny. The jaw is angular.

The hoodie is oversized and dusty indigo. Its hood forms a collar mass behind the neck. The shoulders extend wider than the body. Both arms are crossed over a kangaroo pocket. Two white drawstrings sit on the sides: the left one shorter, the right one longer with a frayed end. The hem is uneven.

The teen’s right sleeve is pushed up, exposing a black forearm with a scratched panel and an orange primer chip. Under the hoodie, his legs are slim: the left leg points straight toward the family, while the right leg is bent and its foot turned out. The left shoe is slightly lifted at the heel, its lace untied and trailing; the pet’s nose is aimed at that loose lace. Both chunky off-white shoes have thick soles and magenta side stripes, but one sole carries a circular tread pattern while the other stripe is scuffed.

The crossed arms are tucked, but the thumb of the raised arm shows a hex nut ring echoing the washer jewelry. The chest lamp is mostly hidden by the hoodie and arms, leaking only a faint magenta glow from the collar. The teen’s weight rests on his straight leg; his hip is cocked out to the right and his shoulder toward the family is raised, while his head tilts away. His foot aimed at the family turns outward to give the pet room.

The child’s head sits at (820, 660), slightly overlapping the mother’s skirt and to the left of the pet. It is a large circle with radius 72. A bent spring antenna with a yellow bead rests on top. The face is blue. The eyes are huge white circles with dark pupils and star catchlights, looking upward at the camera. The brows are high arcs showing excitement. One cheek is a red circle, but the image-right one is smeared downward as if from a scratch or messy paint.

The child’s mouth is an open rounded rectangle with a dark interior, three tooth rectangles stacked above it, and the middle one missing to create a gap. The child’s ears are small yellow circles.

The body is small and rounded in blue. A bright chest lamp sits on its torso and will cycle through colors. The image-left arm reaches toward the mother’s apron string. The image-right arm is raised in a wave with a bent elbow and four spread fingers; this arm breaks the formal front line.

The child’s waving arm will carry a faint ghost afterimage at twenty percent opacity to suggest motion in the still frame. Its legs are short and yellow, with one knee wrapped in a beige bandage that looks slightly peeling. The image-left arm is tinted with a darker yellow (#e6b422) to mark it as a replaced part. Both feet are yellow boots with cyan soles; the image-right sole is lit while the left remains dark, and the child stands on books.

The books are two blank rectangles with colored insets. The bottom one is maroon and thicker. The top one is olive and rotated -3 degrees so the stack tilts and the child leans. They sit in front of the mother's skirt. Their height is excessive, which is the joke. The mother steadies the child with her hand on their back.

The pet is a low robot dog in front of the teen’s left foot, to the right of the books. Its body is a long teal capsule with four stubby legs and wheels. The head sits at the left end, big relative to the body, with its snout aimed at the loose shoelace. One ear hangs floppy while the other perks up asymmetrically. Its eyes are large and slightly crossed, looking up-left at the lace. A dark nose with a highlight completes its face.

The pet’s mouth is slightly open with a pink ribbon tongue showing visible cable ridges. Its coral collar holds a dented blank tag. A thick segmented cable tail curves up and down toward the corner, ending in a plug; it appears mid-wag in the still frame and can rotate slightly as an animation. The blink animation is being refined. A vertical ellipse scaling its height from zero would leave a faint line at rest, and opacity alone would make the lid pop in rather than close smoothly. A scaleY transform on a group element is now being considered to create a more natural closing motion.

The blink animation is being refined. A vertical ellipse scaling from the center would cover the eye outward, which looks unnatural. Instead, a rectangle or ellipse positioned at the top of the eye will have its height animated to create a proper closing lid. A clip-path is being added to keep the lid strictly inside the eye circle.

The blink animation is now a vertical rectangle whose height scales from zero to the eye diameter, clipped strictly inside the eye circle so it closes smoothly from the top. Grandpa’s small eye will blink while his large eye stays permanently open, creating a comically mismatched pair. Mom will blink both eyes together at a slow pace. The kid may not blink at all, since excitement keeps its eyes wide.

The teen will blink only his visible eye, very slowly. Dad will never blink, which is uncanny. The lid animation will stay at zero height when idle so the static frame does not show closed eyes. Clip paths will get unique IDs, and ampersands will be avoided to prevent XML issues.

The full SVG will be written in one pass so the first preview shows the complete composition. Coordinates will be rounded for cleanliness, and the floor line is fixed at y=878.

The first screenshot will be critiqued as an art director to check if the portrait reads clearly in two seconds, whether faces are legible, and if awkwardness is visible. The code will be kept tight while preserving all details. The wooden chair post is being placed at x=155, y=455 with dimensions 16 by 423.

The right chair post is being shortened to y=858 so the leg rests on the coaster. A folded cloth ellipse at y=868 will sit beneath the leg to make the offset obvious.

The chair top rail is being drawn as a thick curved wood tube with an ink outline behind it. Two slats will run from the rail down to the seat.

The chair seat will be an ellipse with a stroke. Grandpa will sit in front of it, his boots in front and his torso covering the center. A burgundy cushion ellipse with an off-center button will sit on the seat. The code will live in `src/build_portrait.py` and be written in one pass.

The visual style is being refined to blend Wes Anderson symmetry with broken, awkward subjects. The backdrop will be symmetrical yet deliberately disrupted by seams and a reflector corner. Warm colors against the cool gray background will feel expensive. Shadows will use a warm brown (#2a211c) instead of pure black to mimic tungsten light.

Contact shadows will use a warm brown fill at 35% opacity, and highlights will be a pale cream. The script will write the finished SVG to `output/awkward-family-portrait.svg` and validate it. A preview flag was considered but set aside in favor of opening Chrome separately.

Limbs will be drawn before joints so the joint circles cover any outline seams cleanly. Grandpa’s outer arm will wrap his cane at x=225, with shoulder at (210, 530), elbow at (190, 640), and hand at (220, 730). His inner arm will run from shoulder at (340, 525) through elbow at (430, 575) to hand at (490, 630).

Mom’s left arm will wrap around x=540 in her lap, with a 35-pixel gap from Grandpa’s hand at x=510. The hand palm sits at 475 and the fingers extend to 505. These coordinates are being locked in explicitly.

The original spacing between grandpa and mom was too wide for a family portrait. Their bodies will be moved closer together, with grandpa centered at 300 and mom at 620.

The final positioning places grandpa at x=300 and mom at x=630, giving a 330-pixel center-to-center gap. Their bodies will sit roughly 110 pixels apart, with the arm crossing the space between them. This creates the intended awkward politeness: not too far to look unrelated, but not so close as to feel comfortable.

Dad is placed at x=810, the teen at 1310, and the kid at 900. The horizontal gap between mom’s head and dad’s head is only 20 pixels because they sit at different heights, so their bodies will almost touch despite the vertical separation.

The vertical gap between dad and mom is 122 pixels, so their heads will not merge. A triangular negative space between dad's chin, mom's bun, and his chest will hold the tie.

The final character centers are fixed at x=300, 630, 810, 900, and 1310. Each robot will be wrapped in an SVG group with a translate transform so the whole portrait can be shifted by adjusting a single wrapper.

Mom’s teeth are being drawn as seven small rectangles along a curve, with the center tooth in a darker gray and the rest in pale cream. The mouth will sit behind them in dark gray.

The kid’s mouth will be open and happy with a gap for a missing tooth. Dad’s LED mouth will be small and pathetic. The teen’s will be a tiny frown. Grandpa’s will be hidden by his mustache. The pet’s will have its tongue out. Six distinct mouth styles will create contrast.

A soft Gaussian blur filter will create contact shadows beneath overlapping foreground elements. Blurred ellipses at the floor level, filled with warm brown at half opacity, will sit under each body to ground the composition.

Shadow ellipses are being sized to match each figure’s footprint. Grandpa gets a 115-pixel radius, mom a 120, dad a 70, the teen a 130, and the kid or cases a 90. The pet shadow is largest and lowest at 150 pixels with its center at y=940, pushing it into the foreground depth. Each ellipse is raised slightly above the floor so the blur does not spill onto the background. The floor will be darkened under the shadows so they remain visible.

The ground line is being dropped to avoid a diagrammatic look. The floor will be created by a large ellipse with a gradient fill and a soft highlight on the curve. Wrinkles are being added to the left side of the background.

The left background is being decorated with uneven paper wrinkles instead of a curtain. A strong dark crease and a faint highlight will sit beside each other, and a seam will run down the center.

A soft light pool will be drawn over the wall behind the characters. It will sit between the seam and the figures so it only tints the backdrop without affecting the robots.

A final warm overlay will be drawn across the entire image from the upper left. It will use a low-opacity blend mode to unify lighting and create a classic photo grade. A vignette and fine grain will be added on top.

The warm overlay will use a soft-light blend mode with 25% opacity and a radial gradient fading from white-warm to transparent. A subtle cool shadow will be added to the lower right corner as part of the vignette. The final look is intended to feel like a printed photograph or illustration. I am now ready to write the code.

The SVG will be written in one complete pass rather than in chunks. The kid’s ghost arm and animation elements are being included. A zero radius on an animated element is being replaced with 0.01 to avoid rendering issues. The file will remain fully detailed and artful.

A headless Chrome command is being prepared to render the SVG and save a screenshot. The workflow will be: generate the file, launch Chrome, capture the image, then read it back.

A preview.html wrapper will reference the SVG for Chrome rendering. qlmanage was considered but rejected in favor of Chrome for accurate filter and blend mode output. The headless screenshot may capture the base frame before SMIL animations begin, so the static pose must look complete on its own.

An HTML img tag will be used to preview the base pose, since it does not execute SMIL animations. The grandpa mustache path is being drawn with a dark brown fill and a lighter stroke, positioned just below his nose.

The grandpa mustache is being detailed with wire curves and two small screws. A nose bolt hexagon sits at (308, 422). The brow ridge is drawn as a squinted, thicker left side.

Grandpa’s ear trumpet is being drawn as a tapered brass horn extending from the right side of his head, with a dark inner tube and two decorative band lines.

The grandpa trumpet will angle upward toward dad’s elbow rather than touching mom. A highlight will be added along the brass horn. The Python script will stay concise while the SVG output remains rich and detailed. An apron bow with two ellipses and two tails is being added to the mom figure.

Mom’s apron bow is being drawn as two rotated ellipses with uneven loops and tails. The bow sits at her left waist, aimed toward grandpa, and may awkwardly fill the gap between them.

The apron bow is placed at mom’s waist, below grandpa’s reaching hand. This vertical separation keeps the bow from colliding with the arm and fills the lower gap without creating a connection. The space between them now holds distinct objects pointing inward: the trumpet above, the open hand in the middle, and the bow, cane, and legs below.

The left side will show almost-connections: grandpa, dad’s stiff hand, and mom’s bow all hover near each other without touching. The center will hold the only real connection—mom holding the kid—while dad’s hand technically touches but awkwardly. The right side will express separation: the teen refuses to bridge, the pet serves as the secret link, and the kid’s wave reaches into the gap but never touches the teen.

The teen will not look at the kid’s wave. Dad’s finger will extend above mom’s shoulder into the gray background so it reads as a silhouette.

content.text: The portrait is a cool gray studio with warm robots who were told to hold still. I’ll draw the relationships in the poses: a hand that doesn’t quite land, a smile held too wide, a wave, and one teenager leaning out of the group.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Awkward robot family portrait.

Five robots and a pet in a studio cyclorama. Relationships are pose and
spacing only: nobody was built as a set, and nobody quite held still.
"""

from pathlib import Path
import math
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

INK = "#1b2126"
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "output" / "awkward-family-portrait.svg"

# Floor line where soles and chair feet land.
FLOOR = 878


def limb(x1, y1, x2, y2, fill, width=26):
    return (
        f'<line x1="{x1}" y1="{y1}" x2="{x2}" y2="{y2}" stroke="{INK}" '
        f'stroke-width="{width + 7}" stroke-linecap="round"/>'
        f'<line x1="{x1}" y1="{y1}" x2="{x2}" y2="{y2}" stroke="{fill}" '
        f'stroke-width="{width}" stroke-linecap="round"/>'
    )


def tube(d, fill, width=16):
    return (
        f'<path d="{d}" fill="none" stroke="{INK}" stroke-width="{width + 7}" '
        f'stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>'
        f'<path d="{d}" fill="none" stroke="{fill}" stroke-width="{width}" '
        f'stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>'
    )


def joint(cx, cy, r, outer, inner="#e4e8ec"):
    return (
        f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r + 2.2}" fill="{INK}"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r}" fill="{outer}"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r * 0.4:.1f}" fill="{inner}"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{cx - r * 0.18:.1f}" cy="{cy - r * 0.22:.1f}" '
        f'r="{r * 0.13:.1f}" fill="#fff" opacity="0.85"/>'
    )


def rivet(x, y, dark="#5a3c18", light="#f6e2b8"):
    return (
        f'<circle cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="3.7" fill="{dark}"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{x - 0.9:.1f}" cy="{y - 1:.1f}" r="1.35" fill="{light}"/>'
    )


def rivets(points, dark="#5a3c18", light="#f6e2b8"):
    return "".join(rivet(x, y, dark, light) for x, y in points)


def spec(cx, cy, rx, ry, op=0.5, rot=-28):
    return (
        f'<ellipse cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" rx="{rx}" ry="{ry}" fill="#fff8ee" '
        f'opacity="{op}" transform="rotate({rot} {cx} {cy})"/>'
    )

        f'r="{max(1.4, r * 0.28):.1f}" fill="#fff" opacity="0.75"/>'
    )


def eye(cx, cy, r, iris, dx=0, dy=0, cloudy=False, lid=None, clip=None):
    """Round glass eye. dx/dy shift the pupil. Catchlight stays upper-left."""
    sclera = "#aebabc" if cloudy else "#f5fafb"
    iris_r = r * (0.62 if cloudy else 0.5)
    pupil_r = r * (0.28 if cloudy else 0.24)
    parts = [
        f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r + 2}" fill="{INK}"/>',
        f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r}" fill="{sclera}"/>',
        f'<circle cx="{cx + dx}" cy="{cy + dy}" r="{iris_r:.1f}" fill="{iris}"/>',
        f'<circle cx="{cx + dx}" cy="{cy + dy}" r="{pupil_r:.1f}" fill="#12161c"/>',
        f'<circle cx="{cx - r * 0.32:.1f}" cy="{cy - r * 0.36:.1f}" '
        f'r="{r * 0.16:.1f}" fill="#fff"/>',
        f'<circle cx="{cx + r * 0.18:.1f}" cy="{cy - r * 0.46:.1f}" '
        f'r="{r * 0.07:.1f}" fill="#fff" opacity="0.85"/>',
    ]
    if lid and clip:
        # Lid grows down from the top of the eye. Resting height is 0.
        parts.append(
            f'<g clip-path="url(#{clip})">'
            f'<rect x="{cx - r - 1}" y="{cy - r - 1}" width="{2 * r + 2}" height="0" '
            f'fill="{lid}">'
            f'<animate attributeName="height" '
            f'values="0;0;{2 * r + 2};0;0" '
            f'keyTimes="0;0.9;0.935;0.97;1" dur="7.5s" '
            f'repeatCount="indefinite"/>'
            f'</rect></g>'
        )
    return "".join(parts)

    """Round glass eye. dx/dy shift the pupil. Catchlight stays upper-left."""
    sclera = "#aebabc" if cloudy else "#f5fafb"

        f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r}" fill="{sclera}"/>',
        f'<circle cx="{cx + dx}" cy="{cy + dy}" r="{iris_r:.1f}" fill="{iris}"/>',
        f'<circle cx="{cx + dx}" cy="{cy + dy}" r="{pupil_r:.1f}" fill="#12161c"/>',
        f'<circle cx="{cx - r * 0.32:.1f}" cy="{cy - r * 0.36:.1f}" '
        f'r="{r * 0.16:.1f}" fill="#fff"/>',
        f'<circle cx="{cx + r * 0.18:.1f}" cy="{cy - r * 0.46:.1f}" '
        f'r="{r * 0.07:.1f}" fill="#fff" opacity="0.85"/>',

    if lid and clip:

        parts.append(
            f'<g clip-path="url(#{clip})">'
            f'<rect x="{cx - r - 1}" y="{cy - r - 1}" width="{2 * r + 2}" height="0" '
            f'fill="{lid}">'
            f'<animate attributeName="height" '

            f'keyTimes="0;0.9;0.935;0.97;1" dur="7.5s" '
            f'repeatCount="indefinite"/>'

    return "".join(parts)

content.text:
An awkward studio portrait of a robot family is in `output/awkward-family-portrait.svg`. Nobody was built as a set, and nobody quite held still.

The brass grandfather sits in his own chair, ear trumpet aimed at the family, one hand stopping short of his daughter-in-law. The father stands behind her with a crooked sash, a half-lit smile, and one finger stuck up off her shoulder. She holds that smile and the child's hand. The flower on her chest has already given up. The child stands on two tool cases and waves. The teenager leans out of the group, arms crossed, one eye covered. The pet bridges the gap, nose on the untied lace, tail plug on the cases.

In a browser the wave, the tail, and that unfinished smile move a little. The still pose is the portrait.
